attributes.previous_value: Four comparisons join the Seraseq reference and paediatric NCH cohort evidence; values cannot be pooled across studies. Tamura et al. 2026 ran 12 short-read callers on haematologic cancer cell lines; one, Genomon, comes from a co-author's group. On 61 driver fusions in conventional RNA-seq of 170 cell lines, Arriba detected all 61 (TPR 1), FusionCatcher 0.98, STAR-Fusion 0.93, InFusion 0.43 and STARChip 0.41. On 24 driver fusions in targeted RNA-seq of 26 cell lines, Arriba again reached 1 and STAR-Fusion 0.92, InFusion 0.17 and STARChip 0. A driver fusion entered these truth sets only if at least four callers, including the one scored, found it and it had literature or RT-PCR support, so fusions that most callers miss are under-represented and these values may overstate sensitivity. Against a consensus of the other callers, the number of single-caller calls, a measure of review burden, ranged on conventional RNA-seq from 327 for TrinityFusion-D and 1,061 for STAR-Fusion (PPV 0.39) to 9,567 for Arriba (PPV 0.08), 22,445 for FusionCatcher and 695,295 for Pizzly. On nanopore long reads from 51 paediatric B-ALL samples (Lin et al. 2026), scored on the dominant fusion per sample, JAFFAL reached sensitivity 0.76, LongGF 0.70 and FusionSeeker 0.63, with precision 0.79 to 0.95; the authors' own FUSILLI reached 0.81. At about one tenth of the depth, sensitivity was 0.09 to 0.27. In an independent long-read benchmark (Dorney et al. 2026 preprint), no caller exceeded F1 0.35 on 400 simulated fusions at 100 Gb and 95% read identity: CTAT-LR-Fusion 0.35 (recall 0.28, precision 0.46), JAFFAL 0.29, Genion 0.20, FusionSeeker 0.14, GFSeeker 0.07 and LongGF 0.04. On all ONT PCR-cDNA reads of the MCF7 cell line, CTAT-LR-Fusion's calls matched 20 of 53 previously reported fusions, with 51 other calls; JAFFAL matched 19 with 38 other calls and FusionSeeker 11 with 359. The other calls mix real fusions missing from the literature list and false calls. On the Huh7 cell line, pooling six long-read callers per long-read platform and three short-read callers for Illumina, PacBio Kinnex recovered 20 of 34 previously reported fusions, ONT PCR-cDNA 17 and Illumina 15. Against karyotyping, FISH and RT-PCR in 101 adult and paediatric acute leukaemia patients (Kim et al. 2025), an Arriba workflow with manual review detected 40 of 48 conventionally detected fusions (sensitivity 83.3%) and called fusions in 21.4% of 56 conventionally negative results; these count against specificity, although the authors describe several as well-known recurrent fusions and confirmed one by RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing. These are cell lines, simulations and leukaemia samples: no linked comparison covers solid-tumour specimens, FFPE tissue or novel-fusion discovery, only Kim et al. score against orthogonal clinical assays, none reports interval estimates, and none establishes clinical performance.

attributes.endpoint: TP, FP, FN, TPR, PPV and F1 for driver fusions on targeted RNA-seq of haematologic cell lines for 12 algorithms
attributes.rationale: Validated driver fusions in real RNA-seq of haematologic cancer cell lines directly measure each caller's sensitivity for clinically relevant fusions. The truth set was selected partly by caller agreement, and one of the 12 algorithms (Genomon) is from a co-author's group.
constraints: Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator before citing a result.
Do not combine this mapping's evaluations with any other protocol's results; truth sets, specimens, sequencing and caller versions differ between sources.
limitations: Haematologic cancer cell lines only (170 for conventional, 26 for targeted RNA-seq); no solid tumours, FFPE tissue or clinical specimens. Per-caller results on 165 clinical samples are only in a figure.

Circular truth selection: a driver pair entered the truth set only if four or more of the 12 algorithms detected it, counting the algorithm being scored, and it was reported in the literature; 2 pairs from the conventional analysis were added (Methods 'Comparison of detection algorithms'). Driver fusions that most callers miss are therefore under-represented, so TPR may overstate sensitivity.

False positives are listed driver fusions detected by one algorithm only; listed driver calls by two or three algorithms that are not in the truth set count as neither TP nor FP, so the driver PPV understates review burden.
Truth: 24 driver fusion-cell line pairs (17 unique fusions); with 24 pairs, one fusion moves TPR by about 0.04.
Targeted assay is the authors' own hybridisation-capture panel (44 fusion-target genes and 134 known fusion junctions).
Genomon rows are author_reported: a co-author is first author of the Genomon fusion paper; the other 11 algorithms were developed elsewhere.
Default or recommended parameters only; the authors show that parameter changes recover some missed driver fusions (Results).
